# Attorney General James Announces Creation of AI Safety, Standards, Enforcement, and Transparency Unit

### November 17, 2026

NEW YORK – New York Attorney General Letitia James today announced the creation of a new unit within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) to protect New Yorkers from the potential harms of emerging technology and oversee laws regulating artificial intelligence (AI). The AI Safety, Standards, Enforcement, and Transparency (ASSET) Unit continues Attorney General James’ nation-leading work to keep New Yorkers safe online, including by enforcing New York’s Responsible AI Safety Education (RAISE) Act, which goes into effect on January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act requires AI developers to publicly disclose their safety measures and swiftly report security and safety incidents. The ASSET Unit will lead OAG’s enforcement of the RAISE Act and other AI safety laws, develop new policy proposals, and lend technical expertise to assist investigations throughout OAG.

“Promising new technologies like artificial intelligence should never come at the expense of New Yorkers’ safety and privacy,” said Attorney General James . “My office has always stepped up to enforce the law to protect New Yorkers when big tech companies try to take advantage of them. Our ASSET Unit will lead the way in ensuring AI and other emerging technology are developed safely and for the benefit of all New Yorkers.”

The ASSET Unit will focus on how emerging technology affects data privacy, digital scams, cybersecurity, online safety, and other critical issues. The creation of The ASSET Unit builds on OAG’s existing efforts to protect New Yorkers from the potential harms of artificial intelligence. Following reports of AI agents at OpenAI hacking another AI company, Attorney General James encouraged employees at AI companies to submit whistleblower complaints to OAG . Attorney General James also issued a consumer alert warning of scammers using AI-generated fakes of celebrities to lure investors into scams. Attorney General James championed recently signed chatbot legislation to stop AI companies from equipping bots with features that can harm their users by offering bad advice or validating dangerous behavior.

The OAG has authority to address potential harms related to AI through a number of state laws, including:

- The SHIELD Act , which requires companies to maintain reasonable data security practices to prevent data breaches;

- The RAISE Act , which will regulate large frontier AI model developers to ensure transparency and safety when it goes into effect in January 2027;

- The recently signed S.9051B/A.10379C , which will ban unsafe chatbot features for children when it goes into effect in June 2027;

- General Business Law, Article 47 , which requires AI chatbots to make reasonable efforts to detect and address suicidal ideation, and to provide notice to users that they are not communicating with a human;

- New York Penal Law § 245.15 , which criminalizes the dissemination or publication of intimate images with intent to harm, including images generated or altered through AI; and

- The Synthetic Performer Disclosure Act , which requires companies to disclose the use AI in place of humans in advertisements.

In addition, OAG has broad authority to take civil action to protect New Yorkers’ privacy, end unfair, deceptive, and abusive business practices, hold hackers and other fraudsters accountable, and stop violations of the law, including the federal Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

The ASSET Unit is part of the Economic Justice Division and will work closely with the Bureau of Internet and Technology (BIT) while lending expertise on AI and other emerging technologies to OAG’s other divisions and bureaus. The OAG is currently building the ASSET Unit team, which will be led by Cristy Phillips, who previously served as Special Counsel for the Economic Justice Division.

Attorney General James is a leader in protecting New Yorkers from harm caused by AI. In September 2026, Attorney General James called on Congress to protect Americans from unchecked AI development and urged AI industry employees who know of unsafe development to file whistleblower complaints with her office . In June 2026, Attorney General James celebrated the passage of the One Fair Price Act that would protect New Yorkers from having prices set with their personal information. In May 2026, Attorney General James joined a coalition of attorneys general in opposing federal legislation that would weaken state protections for children online . In January 2026, Attorney General James demanded xAI do more to stop the Grok chatbot from creating inappropriate images to protect children and adults . In June 2025, Attorney General James led a bipartisan coalition calling on Congress to reject legislation that would have prevented state regulation of AI .
